claim.quote: A 30-g xenon bubble chamber, operated at Northwestern University in June and November 2016, has for the first time observed simultaneous bubble nucleation and scintillation by nuclear recoils in a superheated liquid.

key_value_text.quote: We see no evidence for bubble nucleation by gamma rays at any of the thresholds studied, setting a 90% C.L. upper limit of $6.3\times10^{-7}$ bubbles per gamma interaction at a 4.2-keV thermodynamic threshold.

name: First Demonstration of a Scintillating Xenon Bubble Chamber for Detecting Dark Matter and Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
notes: Operated at Northwestern University (not a SNOLAB or Fermilab detector); the SBC collaboration's 2025 paper (arXiv:2410.07241) calls it 'a device filled with pure xenon [that] first demonstrated the ability to operate simultaneously as a bubble chamber and scintillation detector in 2017'.
The paper is not signed 'SBC Collaboration'; its link to the collaboration is the 2025 SBC paper's description of the same device.

summary.plain: A 30-gram xenon bubble chamber at Northwestern University showed for the first time that a superheated liquid can give both a bubble and a flash of light from a nuclear recoil, the idea behind the Scintillating Bubble Chamber.
summary.technical: 30-g xenon chamber with CCD camera, solar-blind PMT for 175-nm scintillation and a piezoelectric acoustic transducer; Seitz thresholds 4.2-15.0 keV; minimum nuclear-recoil energy to nucleate a bubble 19+-6 keV at 8.3 keV; no gamma-ray nucleation, 90% C.L. upper limit 6.3e-7 bubbles per gamma interaction at 4.2 keV (Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 231301). Precursor device, operated before the SBC collaboration's detectors.

title: First Demonstration of a Scintillating Xenon Bubble Chamber for Detecting Dark Matter and Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering
why_it_matters: The abstract says these measurements establish the noble-liquid bubble chamber as a promising new technology for dark matter and CEvNS detection.
